incumbent.name: Jim Tomes
incumbent.summary: Jim Tomes, a Republican from Wadesville, has served in the Senate since 2010 and is seeking a fifth four-year term {tomes_caucus} {wnin_primary}. He chairs the Senate Committee on Veterans Affairs and The Military and is ranking member of Homeland Security and Transportation, according to the Senate Republican caucus {tomes_caucus}.
record: Sept. 16, 2025 and April 8, 2026: Met with CenterPoint Energy executives, including CEO Jason Wells, about constituent complaints over bill increases, month-to-month spikes and smart-meter accuracy {tomes_cnp_2025} {tomes_cnp_2026}.

Nov. 18, 2025: Said in a statement that if redistricting came to a vote, "that vote would then be whether to support our Commander in Chief Donald Trump, or the other party. I would have voted 'yes' for our president" {tomes_redistricting}. WNIN reported that he voted for the redistricting bill in December 2025; it failed in the Senate {wnin_feb} {wiki_2026_senate}.

2026 session: Authored Senate Enrolled Act 176, which bars counties, cities and towns from adopting stricter local rules for shooting ranges than state law; it was ceremonially signed April 29, 2026 {tomes_sea176}. He also authored a bill to study urban microfarm zones; WNIN described him as second author of SB 164 {tomes_2026_sinedie} {wnin_aug}.
2026 session: The Senate Republican caucus reported that he did not miss a floor vote {tomes_caucus}.

June 25, 2026: Named vice-chair of the Interim Study Committee on Public Safety and Military Affairs and a member of the Indiana Veterans' Affairs Commission and the Agriculture and Natural Resources study committee {tomes_study}.

July 17, 2026: In a campaign statement, said he is concerned about losing farmland to data centers but considers siting "primarily a local issue—not a state issue" for county and city officials and property owners {tomes_datacenter}.

race_context: Senate District 49 includes all of Posey County and part of Vanderburgh County, including western Evansville, Mount Vernon, New Harmony and Poseyville; the last Democrat to hold it was Bob Dieg, elected in 2006 {wnin_aug} {clayton_home}.
Tomes had not planned to seek another term but changed his mind, and won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Brandi Durham Pugh with about 80% of the vote {wnin_primary}.
Cindi Clayton filed as the Democratic candidate in early 2026 and is the party's nominee on the Nov. 3 ballot {clayton_blog} {in_list}.

Both candidates name utility bills as a priority: Tomes points to his meetings with CenterPoint, while Clayton says state utility regulation has failed and pledges to take no energy-company money {wnin_aug} {clayton_home}. They also differ on the 2025 redistricting bill, which Tomes voted for and Clayton opposed {wnin_aug}.

The NAACP Evansville Branch and League of Women Voters of Southwestern Indiana invited all local and state candidates to a Sept. 12, 2026 forum in Evansville; coverage confirming which District 49 candidates took part was not found {wnin_forum}. No head-to-head debate was found.

candidates.summary: Clayton is a University of Southern Indiana business communication instructor and chairs the board of Holly's House, an Evansville victim advocacy center {wnin_aug} {clayton_ballotready}. She lists public-school funding, utility costs and responsiveness to constituents as her priorities {clayton_home}.
background: Has taught business communication at USI since 2002 and runs a leadership coaching and HR consulting firm; earlier worked in human resources, according to her BallotReady profile {clayton_ballotready}.
Holds a bachelor's degree in psychology and a master's in communication from USI and describes herself as a 30-year Evansville resident {clayton_ballotready} {clayton_home}.
Board chair of Holly's House, a child and adult victim advocacy center {wnin_aug}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Democratic candidate in January 2026; she wrote that she knew of no primary challenger at the time {clayton_blog}. She is the Democratic nominee on the Nov. 3 ballot {in_list}.

items: Says fully funding public schools would be her first priority and supports restoring income limits for school vouchers {wnin_aug} {clayton_home}.
Says Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission oversight of CenterPoint "is simply not working" and pledges to refuse campaign money from energy companies {clayton_home}.
Opposed the 2025 congressional redistricting effort and said local residents who opposed it "weren't listened to" {wnin_aug}.
Supports barring elected officials from signing non-disclosure agreements {wnin_aug}.
Plans weekly office hours, answering her own email and attending neighborhood meetings outside session {wnin_aug}.

on_incumbent: On her campaign site, Clayton writes that Tomes "has had 15+ years in office to act on energy gouging yet has chosen not to do so" {clayton_home}.
Told WNIN she would represent "only the constituents of district 49 — not federal administration, not a corporate sponsor" {wnin_aug}.
plans: Says restoring public-school funding would be her most important priority {clayton_home}.
Would hold weekly office hours if elected {wnin_aug}.
endorsements_finance: Her campaign site says she is endorsed by the United Mine Workers of America {clayton_home}.
gaps: Her campaign site's About page returned a not-found error; background comes from WNIN, BallotReady and her home page.
A WEHT story on her November 2025 campaign launch was cited by Wikipedia but not read.
No statements found on property taxes, data centers or the 2025 state budget.

candidates.summary: Tomes, a Vietnam veteran and retired Teamster truck driver, has represented the district since 2010 {tomes_caucus}. He emphasizes personal responsiveness to constituents and lowering utility bills {wnin_aug}.
background: Served in the U.S. Army with the 101st Airborne Division in Vietnam; worked 33 years as a truck driver and was a union steward for 21 years, according to the Senate Republican caucus {tomes_caucus}.
Director of the 2nd Amendment Patriots and past commander of Wadesville VFW Post 6576; lives near Blairsville {tomes_caucus} {tomes_about}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Brandi Durham Pugh with about 80% of the vote {wnin_primary}.

items: Says getting something done on utility bills is a priority and cites his meetings with CenterPoint leadership {wnin_aug} {tomes_cnp_2026}.
Says he is concerned about the loss of farmland, recognizes possible construction jobs and investment, and views siting decisions as mainly for local officials and property owners {tomes_datacenter}.
Supported the 2025 redistricting effort and told WNIN constituents were divided on it {tomes_redistricting} {wnin_aug}.
Authored SEA 176 (2026) limiting local regulation of shooting ranges {tomes_sea176}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. He told WNIN, "I take all my calls, all my emails, all my handwritten letters, and respond to everyone personally" {wnin_aug}. No statements by Tomes about Clayton were found.
plans: Told WNIN he has "six or seven bills" in mind, including one setting aside two days of youth hunting season for children with disabilities, and further action on utility bills {wnin_aug}.
endorsements_finance: His campaign lists endorsements from the Indiana State AFL-CIO, Indiana Farm Bureau, Indiana FOP, NRA Political Victory Fund, NFIB Indiana PAC, Indiana Right to Life PAC, several building-trades and steelworkers unions, and U.S. Sen. Jim Banks {tomes_endorse}.
Wikipedia's 2026 Indiana Senate election page lists President Donald Trump and Gov. Mike Braun as endorsing him {wiki_2026_senate}.
gaps: His votes on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) and the 2025 state budget were not verified.
Wikipedia lists primary results of 2,529 (81.8%) for Tomes to 562 (18.2%) for Pugh under a table mislabeled District 43; not confirmed against official results.
